subject: VPC handback verification runbook
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@healthcorp.com>

Cc: HealthCorp Legal <legal@healthcorp.com>; Procurement <procurement@healthcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC handback — verification requirements

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for walking us through the Private VPC handback options last week. As we move toward contract close (HC-9843), Legal has asked for a short, prescriptive verification runbook we can include in the SOW. The core asks are:

- Step-by-step evidence checklist for tenant data destruction (snapshots, objects, backups)
- Timeline for attestations and evidence delivery
- What artifacts we will receive (logs, deletion receipts, snapshot hashes) and how long you'll retain those artifacts
- Any limitations where Redwood cannot provide a particular artifact immediately (e.g., underlying cloud provider constraints)

Can you provide a single-runbook doc and a suggested acceptance criteria matrix we can sign off on? We need something Legal can review by EOD Thursday.

Appreciate it —
Lina
Lina Park
Head of Cloud Security, HealthCorp
lina.park@healthcorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@healthcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>; Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC handback — verification requirements

Hi Lina —

Thanks — attached is a first-pass runbook and an XLS checklist tailored to HealthCorp's scope. High level summary:

1) What we provide
- A runbook (PDF) with step-by-step operations for tenant handback (object store purge, snapshot tombstoning, KV cache purge, metadata tombstones).
- Deletion receipts: signed metadata receipts (SHA256 hashes of deleted snapshot manifests) and operation logs for each step.
- Audit bundle: log bundle (syslog + auditd) and KMS key rotation/disable events where applicable.

2) Typical timeline
- Day 0: scheduling, runbook acceptance (signed SOW addendum)
- Day 1–3: pre-handback snapshot and evidence generation; customer review window
- Day 4–7: destructive operations (object purge + metadata wipe) and immediate receipts
- Day 8–14: final attestations and archival of evidence (kept for 90 days for handback records unless otherwise agreed)

3) Limitations/notes
- For on-prem/backed storage islands where HealthCorp manages storage, Redwood will provide operation logs and guidance but cannot execute physical destruction.
- If an external cloud provider enforces delayed snapshot deletion (retention window), we will provide deletion receipts once the provider completes the purge; runbook defines compensating controls and timelines.

I left inline acceptance criteria in the checklist file (attachment). If that looks good, I suggest we capture acceptance as a short SOW addendum and attach the runbook.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_handback_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF), healthcorp_handback_checklist_v1.xlsx (XLSX)

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Security Programs | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@healthcorp.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC handback — verification requirements

Looping in a few technical clarifications for the runbook (Lina: feel free to skip).

- Deletion artifacts: we will publish one signed manifest per destructive operation. Each manifest contains the list of object keys, a SHA256 digest, and the Redwood operator ID that initiated the job. Manifest is signed with our service signing key; we can provide the public key material in the audit bundle.
- Snapshots: we create a tombstone entry and then issue provider delete calls. For providers that enforce retention windows, the manifest will show the issued delete call and a later "provider confirmed purge" receipt.
- KMS: we will rotate customer-bound data keys where customers use Redwood-managed keys; for customer-managed keys (BYOK) we will flag any key-handling steps we cannot perform and provide the rotation/disable event logs.
- Proof window: we keep the audit bundles for 90 days after handback by default; if HealthCorp needs longer retention of the evidence bundle for its own compliance, we can extend to 1 year under the enterprise addendum.

I added a short tech appendix to the runbook in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRD-handback-runbook

-Karthik
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@healthcorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC handback — verification requirements

Lina — small additions I recommend for Legal's acceptance criteria:

- Acceptance metric: HealthCorp signs the received manifest hashes within 48 hours of receipt to acknowledge evidence integrity; if no response, Redwood will retain manifests and log a nondelivery event.
- Operational SLA: destructive operations will be scheduled into a blackout window agreed 48 hours in advance; emergency accelerations possible with signed approval.
- Escrow option: if HealthCorp needs longer evidence retention, include an escrow clause (we can escrow the signed manifests with a third-party registrar).

If those are acceptable I'll update the checklist and prepare a one-paragraph SOW addendum suitable for DocuSign.

-Jonas
